claims.text: Controlled post-synthesis annealing can promote fine nanoscale twin-boundary formation in MnNiSi-based alloys.
Fine twin-boundary formation induced by annealing will improve the toughness of MnNiSi-based alloys.
Post-synthesis microstructural refinement will improve fatigue resistance.
Standard rapid-solidification or as-cast synthesis of MnNiSi-based alloys produces a coarse-grained microstructure with relatively few twin boundaries.
Annealing below the magnetic transition temperature can refine the grain structure and induce nanoscale twin boundaries.
Keeping the annealing temperature below the magnetic transition temperature will avoid alteration of magnetic exchange interactions.
The controlled annealing process will reduce grain size in addition to forming fine twin boundaries.
Nanoscale twin boundaries impede dislocation motion.
Impeded dislocation motion caused by nanoscale twin boundaries improves mechanical strength.
Refined microstructural features, including grain-size and grain-boundary characteristics, are associated with fatigue performance in metallic materials.
Magnetic exchange pathways will remain largely unaffected by the proposed twin-boundary and grain-size changes.
Preserving magnetic exchange pathways will preserve the large magnetic entropy change.
Annealed MnNiSi-based alloys will have greater toughness than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed MnNiSi-based alloys will have longer fatigue life than the as-cast baseline.
The magnetic entropy change of annealed samples will remain within approximately 10% of that of untreated samples.
As-cast MnNiSi-based alloys have acceptable magnetocaloric properties but limited mechanical durability.
Unwanted phase changes or compositional shifts caused by excessive annealing could compromise the magnetocaloric effect.
Appropriate post-treatment can reduce premature fatigue failure and significantly improve fatigue performance in additively manufactured metallic parts.
